scope: Reviewed context anchors for the 1.8 to Spectron 2.2 ARM64 cross-build map

evidence: The Spectron function constructs the same encoded a9a marker used by the original premium getter.
It calls the same hash-list codesimplefix0 and decodesimple helpers before clearing and returning the string.
The translated Spectron sigcheck function calls this candidate while checking the premium marker.
Two other normalized-shape candidates exist, but they do not share this marker construction or sigcheck context.
anchors.source_basis: encoded marker, helper calls, and caller context

evidence: The Spectron function returns the one-byte gtGCDail9W state field.
The mapped Spectron setter at 0x1603bc writes the same gtGCDail9W field.
The mapped Spectron QPlayLoop calls this getter before choosing the loading-screen or game rendering path.
The original getter is the matching one-byte accessor for the loading-screen state.
anchors.source_basis: getter/setter field pairing and QPlayLoop caller context

evidence: The Spectron function is the target of all Connecting to the server, Connecting to %s, StartConnectMessage, and language-string references.
It has the same 39 basic-block and 40 direct-call shape as the original connecting-window function.
Its instruction count is 240 versus 235 in the original, consistent with a rebuilt version of the same UI path.
anchors.source_basis: connecting-window string references and control-flow shape

evidence: The Spectron ARM64 dynamic symbol is the same JNI export name as the original.
The function selects the loading-screen or world rendering path using the translated loading-screen getter.
The function remains a direct runtime anchor even though its rebuilt body is shorter.
anchors.source_basis: exact JNI export name and loading/world render control flow

interpretation: These rows are reviewed cross-build correspondences, not recovered original debug symbols.
The v18_ prefix marks a 1.8 semantic label applied to a Spectron 2.2 function address.
The address and obfuscated target name remain recorded so every label can be audited against the supplied Spectron binary.
